name: olp-distinct-groupby-alias
tables: CREATE TABLE t (id BIGINT NOT NULL, a BIGINT, b BIGINT, PRIMARY KEY (id))

groups.name: distinct_idempotent
groups.reason: DISTINCT is idempotent: distinct of an already-distinct set (or of a plain projection) yields the same multiset; NULLs collapse to a single NULL row in every form
queries: SELECT DISTINCT a FROM (SELECT DISTINCT a FROM t) s
SELECT DISTINCT a FROM (SELECT a FROM t) s

groups.name: distinct_eq_groupby
groups.reason: SELECT DISTINCT a and GROUP BY a produce the same set of distinct a values; SQL GROUP BY puts all NULLs in one group, matching DISTINCT's single NULL row
queries: SELECT a FROM t GROUP BY a

groups.name: distinct_multicol_eq_groupby
groups.reason: multi-column DISTINCT equals GROUP BY on the same columns; each (a,b) combination appears once, NULL treated as a single group value per column
queries: SELECT DISTINCT a, b FROM t
SELECT a, b FROM t GROUP BY a, b

groups.name: alias_invariance
groups.reason: column aliases are cosmetic; the produced row values are identical regardless of the alias name or its absence
queries: SELECT a AS x, b AS y FROM t
SELECT a AS foo, b AS anything_here FROM t

groups.name: groupby_orderby_null_placement_BUG
groups.reason: ENGINE-BUG SENTINEL (expected to fail until fixed): both queries return the identical relation (the distinct values of a = {5,7,NULL}) under the identical ORDER BY a ASC, so they must produce the identical ordered sequence. They do not: DISTINCT+ORDER BY orders NULL FIRST (consistent with FDB tuple encoding, where NULL sorts before all values, and with the plain-scan ORDER BY path), while GROUP BY+ORDER BY orders NULL LAST. NULL placement under ORDER BY ASC is a property of the ORDER BY clause, not of the chosen plan, so this internal inconsistency is an engine defect in the GROUP BY aggregation+sort path.
queries: SELECT DISTINCT a FROM t ORDER BY a
SELECT a FROM t GROUP BY a ORDER BY a
